Class JdbcDataTypeConversionTables

java.lang.Object
dev.visdb.seesaw.datasources.JdbcDataTypeConversionTables
public class JdbcDataTypeConversionTables extends Object
Data Type Conversion Tables; Appendix B of JDBC 4.2 Specification JSR 221, March 2014. In this class the tables are usually ImmutableListMultimaps, jdbcTypeToClass is an exception, it's based on an EnumMap. In addition to the tables, there is a method with the same name as the table which takes a key as a parameter and generally returns the first item in the list; see jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType) for an exception.

Table B.3 is updated for the java1.8 and later world.

  • Field Details

    • jdbcTypeToClass

      public static final Map<JDBCType, Collection<Class<?>>> jdbcTypeToClass
      Map JdbcType to Java Object; JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 3.

      Implementation note:

      The JDBC 4.2 spec only has one class listed per JDBCType since they are the types returned by getObject for a given type. However, for certain types (not constrained to JDBC 1.0) newer JDK types are recommended and of course there are the new *WITH_TIMEZONE types. Since this is a list multimap, the updated information is included and is provided by the default method jdbcTypeToClass(java.sql.JDBCType); see that method's javadoc for the details of the change. To get strict adherence to the spec, use jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType)

    • classToJdbcType

      public static final com.google.common.collect.ImmutableListMultimap<Class<?>,JDBCType> classToJdbcType
      Map Java Object to JdbcTypes; JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 4

      Note that the elements of the map are a list. Typically use the method classToJdbcType(java.lang.Class) which returns the first JDBCType for the class with ClassToJDBCType.get(Some.class).get(0) to get an item.

  • Method Details

    • jdbcTypeToClass

      public static Class<?> jdbcTypeToClass(JDBCType type)
      Map JdbcType to Java Object Class; JDBC 4.2 spec, Appendix B Table 3.

      The differences from spec with their return values are

      • TINYINT Byte
      • SMALLINT Short
      • DATE java.time.LocalDate
      • TIME java.time.LocalTime
      • TIMESTAMP java.time.LocalDateTime
      • TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE java.time.OffetTime
      • TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE java.time.OffetDateTime

      Note that TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE and TIMESTAMP_WITH_TIMEZONE are not found at all in Table 3.

      Use jdbcTypeToClassStrict(java.sql.JDBCType) for strict adherence to the spec.

      Parameters:
      type - JDBCType
      Returns:
      corresponding java object class
